clue.text: Measure to control traffic, more or less

approximately, as in '... fifty people came'

clue.text: Aid rules broken regarding leftover material

explanation.surface: Breaking the rules on financial aid, as it concerns surplus stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what remains after a process, so this noun names material left over.

clue.text: Vague relative starts to act rashly

parts.note: an uncle is a family relative

indicators.note: the starts of the words act and rashly supply their opening letters

explanation.surface: A relative whose thinking is muddled begins behaving recklessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vague is indistinct or not plainly expressed, a close synonym.

clue.text: With passion, this writer enters to reject dejection

rage is a violent passion
the setter referring to themselves gives ME

clue.text: Beadle, followed by his leader, summoned by this buzzer

explanation.walkthrough: A beadle was a minor parish officer in Britain; Dickens's Mr Bumble is the famous one. The letter B, called out, is spoken 'bee'.
explanation.definitionFit: A large furry social insect that hums loudly as it flies, hence a buzzer.

clue.text: Take power from sharpshooter, but not at first

indicators.note: the opening letter of the shooter's word is not included, so it is dropped from the front

parts.note: a gunman is a person armed with a gun, a marksman

explanation.surface: Disarming a sniper, though not right at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To unman someone is to deprive them of strength or courage, sapping their power.

clue.text: Prophet, a Biblical figure, for the most part

parts.note: Moses is the Old Testament leader who received the Commandments

explanation.surface: A prophet described as mostly a figure from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is one of the minor Old Testament prophets, with a book named after him.

clue.text: Composer not involved in revolutionary piece

parts.note: an item is a single piece, as in an item of news

explanation.definitionFit: Gian Carlo Menotti was an Italian-American composer of operas such as Amahl and the Night Visitors.

clue.text: Sun's to hang around, providing night-time illumination

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for Sunday, the Sun's day

explanation.surface: The sun is going to linger, lighting up the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' looks like the star itself, but here it stands for Sunday, abbreviated S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sky full of stars is lit by them after dark, so starry describes that night-time light.

clue.text: Basic stuff: book to study and book to publish

parts.note: B is again the abbreviation for book
to read a subject is to study it, as in reading law
taken as written

to utter can mean to put into circulation or make public

explanation.surface: A student's routine of reading one book and putting out another.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you 'read' a subject at university, meaning study it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread-and-butter matters are the everyday essentials, the routine core of something.

clue.text: Knocks footwear

definitions.meaning: punches or hits, as a verb
garments worn on the feet inside shoes

clue.text: Notes? Third in scale excited no drama

clue.text: Mistakenly count blonde's head as hazel

the head of the word blonde is its first letter

clue.text: Mexican to pass on in two ways

clue.text: City Road filled with actors, right?

indicators.note: the road word is filled with the actors, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road
the cast is the set of actors in a show

explanation.surface: A city street packed with performers, rightly so.
explanation.walkthrough: LANCASTER is a historic city in northwest England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancaster is a county town and city in Lancashire, England.

clue.text: A dull fellow in exam a university runs initially is producing a glowing display

indicators.note: the initial letters of a, university and runs are taken
the dull fellow and the article go inside the spoken exam

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
a bore is a tedious person

clue.text: Made further corrections — and paper ran out

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets
ended means came to a stop or ran out

clue.text: Excitement? This year shows excitement

explanation.definitionFit: Hysteria is wild uncontrolled emotion, an extreme form of agitated excitement.

clue.text: How one gets winnings from a one-armed bandit?

definitions.text: How one gets winnings from a one-armed bandit?

parts.words: How one gets winnings from a one-armed bandit?

explanation.walkthrough: A one-armed bandit is a slot machine; the jackpot comes from working it with one hand, which literally means doing it without help.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with one hand alone, unaided, is the idiom for working without help.

clue.text: Evil period brought up by start of life of crime

clue.text: Boy catching vermin held up about ten

clue.text: Insect's attention given to rug
